Name: Dell Command | Update
Description: Dell's driver, firmware and BIOS update client, wrapped so the deployment itself has a version Intune can compare.
Awkwardness: Installing Dell Command | Update is not the same as updating anything. The work is done afterwards by dcu-cli.exe on a schedule, so a fleet can be one hundred per cent compliant on this application and still be a year behind on firmware. The installer also has a habit of removing what it considers conflicting Dell software (Dell Update, Dell SupportAssist for PCs are the usual casualties), which is the correct behaviour and still a surprise if nobody was told. Dell ships the application in two flavours - the classic Win32 build and the Universal Windows Platform build - which land in different folders and carry different uninstall strings, so a detection or uninstall rule written against one silently does nothing on the other.
DownloadNotes: Dell's download page requires you to pick a flavour. Note which one you took - Universal Windows Platform or classic - because the install path and uninstall string differ.
Notes: NOT tested in this repository. The switches below are transcribed from Dell's documentation, which is usually right and occasionally a release out of date.
Run 'msimaker analyze <installer>' against your actual download first: the fingerprint confirms the installer family, and so the switches.
Dell documents /s for a silent install and a /l=<file> logging switch. Neither has been run here. Try them by hand on one device before deploying.

No uninstall action is wired up, deliberately. Dell Command | Update registers its own entry in Programs and Features and this package cannot guess the uninstall string; read it out of the registry on a test device, then add a Run action with Command and When: Uninstall.

What you probably want next is a scheduled task running dcu-cli.exe, which lives under Program Files\Dell\CommandUpdate. Its switches changed between DCU 4 and DCU 5, so check the Dell Command | Update reference guide for the version you deployed rather than copying a command from a blog. A scheduled task in this project cannot reference dcu-cli.exe anyway: a task's executable must be part of the payload.

Arp.Comments: Dell Command | Update wrapped as an MSI. Silent switches from vendor documentation, untested.
